note: Synthetic results passed through Prowler's real finding and OCSF output code. Real CLI exports carry time_dt in the scanning machine's local time without an offset; these carry UTC with an offset.

fixtures.description: Account A, first scan: PASS, FAIL, MANUAL and muted results; global (IAM) and regional resources; two access keys sharing one ARN; one ARN reported in two regions.
Account A, a week later: fixes, a PASS-to-FAIL regression, a missing resource (sg-0a1), a muted PASS, and the two regions of one ARN moving in opposite directions.
The T2 scan exported again: the same observations in a different order with a different random scan ID. Semantically identical to aws-a-t2-followup, but not byte-identical.
Account A, third scan: k9-logs fails again after being fixed, sg-0a1 comes back as MANUAL, root MFA passes.
Claims the same scan time as aws-a-t2-followup but reports k9-logs as FAIL: a conflict.
Account B, first scan, with a security group ID that also exists in account A.
Accounts A and B in one file, each with its own scan time.
Two different resources (different ARNs) with the same check, account, region and resource name. Prowler gives both the same finding UID; K9 must keep them apart.
The same observation twice in one file (identical content).
The same resource and check twice in one scan with different results.
An Azure finding. K9 V1 supports AWS only and must reject it.
